framework.primary_law: Federal Council AI regulatory strategy (12 February 2025): sector-specific approach and ratification of the Council of Europe AI Convention
framework.enforcing_body: Federal Department of Justice and Police and sector regulators; Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner
framework.geographic_scope: Existing Swiss law applies; no horizontal AI law planned.

source_documents.title: Switzerland Sets Its Course on AI Legislation
AI Regulation Switzerland, 2026 Status and Outlook

research.summary: On 12 February 2025 the Federal Council chose a sector-specific, technology-neutral approach and rejected an EU-style horizontal AI law. Its priority is to ratify the Council of Europe AI Convention, with a consultation draft expected by end 2026, plus non-binding measures such as self-declaration frameworks. Ratification needs parliamentary approval and may face a referendum.

key_provisions.title: Council of Europe Convention ratification
key_provisions.description: Incorporate the binding AI Convention into Swiss law.

key_provisions.title: Sector-specific adjustments
key_provisions.description: Targeted changes where fundamental rights are affected.

cross_jurisdiction_tensions.tension: Swiss exporters of high-risk AI must meet EU conformity assessment because mutual recognition remains blocked.

safety_risk_management.rationale: No mandatory AI risk framework planned.

privacy_data_protection.rationale: Data protection law is strong and applies to AI.

fairness_non_discrimination.rationale: Personality rights and anti-discrimination law apply.

access_to_remedy.rationale: Courts and the data commissioner provide recourse.

gaps_and_weaknesses: Consultation draft not yet published as of the sources used.
research.monitor_notes: Check whether the end-2026 consultation draft on the AI Convention has been published. Scores are provisional AI-drafted judgements against the AIETHOS rubric and reflect protections currently in force.

citizen.one_line: Switzerland will not copy the EU's AI Act; it plans to adopt the Council of Europe treaty and adjust sector laws.
citizen.what_changed: Switzerland decided in February 2025 to take a light-touch route. A draft law to adopt the Council of Europe AI treaty is expected by the end of 2026.
citizen.who_is_protected: People in Switzerland through data protection and personality rights.
who_is_not_protected: People harmed by AI in sectors with no targeted rules yet

your_rights.what_it_means: The revised Data Protection Act gives rights over personal data and automated individual decisions.
your_rights.how_to_invoke: Contact the controller, then the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner.

citizen.plain_language_summary: Switzerland is taking a gradual approach, relying on existing laws and an international treaty.

jargon_buster.Technology-neutral: Rules that apply regardless of the specific technology.
